open_points.subject: A18 retention cutoff time source
open_points.text: The step reads the clock once, before it looks at any file, and its cutoff is that UTC instant less exactly 720 hours.
open_points.question: Which clock supplies this UTC instant, and is it the same UTC wall-clock source used for recorded backup instants?
options: Read the process's UTC wall clock once when the third step starts.
Derive the cutoff from a monotonic clock anchored to an earlier UTC reading.
Use a separately injected retention clock whose relationship to the backup-recording clock is specified.
open_points.default_guess: Read the same UTC wall-clock source used for backup instants once at the start of the third step.

open_points.subject: A18 backup instant representation and precision
open_points.text: The cutoff and each record's UTC instant (L16) are compared as instants at the full precision each holds, neither rounded nor truncated; a backup whose instant is earlier than the cutoff is deleted.
open_points.question: What concrete representation and precision do the clock reading and stored backup instant have, and how are values with different precisions compared without inventing or discarding fractional time?
options: Store and compare timezone-aware UTC datetimes at a fixed declared fractional-second precision.
Store and compare integer UTC epoch units at a fixed declared resolution.
Allow records of differing resolutions and define the exact normalization and comparison rule.
open_points.default_guess: Use timezone-aware UTC datetimes at one fixed microsecond precision for both clock readings and records.

witness.initial: A kept backup records 2026-10-12T12:00:00.400Z; the third step starts on 2026-11-11 near 12:00:00Z.
events: Registry reads a cutoff-source value that can represent 2026-11-11T12:00:00.500Z.
Registry compares the stored instant with the value 720 hours earlier.
outcomes: With fractional-second representation, the cutoff is 2026-10-12T12:00:00.500Z and the backup is deleted.
With whole-second clock or storage representation, the cutoff or record becomes 2026-10-12T12:00:00Z and the backup is kept.
witness.observer: The owner inspecting the kept backups or the newest-backup display.

open_points.subject: A18 retention invariant Required test 7
open_points.text:
With the step's cutoff fixed at its start, a kept backup made exactly
   30 × 24 hours before it is kept and one made a second earlier is deleted.
open_points.question: What Required tests item demonstrates that the retention invariant uses the full precision of both instants and does not round or truncate fractional values at the cutoff?
options: Add a case with two instants differing only below one second and require deletion of the earlier one.
Declare a fixed whole-second representation, making subsecond cases impossible.
Expand this item to state the representations and test the smallest representable unit on each side of the cutoff.
open_points.default_guess: Add a fractional-second boundary case using the declared fixed precision.

witness.initial: The implementation truncates both instants to whole seconds before comparison.
events: The test supplies one backup exactly 720 hours old and another 720 hours plus one second old.
The implementation keeps the first and deletes the second.
outcomes: The stated Required test passes even though the implementation truncates instants.
A fractional-boundary test fails and exposes the violation of the full-precision rule.
witness.observer: The test suite and later agents deciding whether the full-precision invariant is proved.
